neighbours.label: relation words in a description of a physiological or cellular mechanism ('preventing', 'of', 'into', 'transports' in sentences about how tissues and cells work), as against the same sentence frames about machines, buildings or trade
fire: The blood-brain barrier blocks many toxins, preventing their entry into neurons.
Hair cells in the inner ear turn vibration into nerve impulses.
Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to the tissues.
Mucus lines the airways, trapping dust and preventing infection of the lungs.
The kidneys filter waste from the blood and return water to the body.
Insulin signals muscle cells to take up glucose from the bloodstream.
The skin acts as a shield, preventing bacteria from reaching deeper tissue.
Platelets gather at the wound and release factors that start clotting.
quiet: The new dam blocks the floodwater, preventing its entry into the town.
Solar panels on the roof turn sunlight into usable power.
Delivery vans carry parcels from the depot to the shops.
Netting covers the orchard, trapping birds and preventing damage to the fruit.
The plant filters waste from the river and returns water to the reservoir.
The thermostat signals the boiler to switch on when the room is cold.
The hedge acts as a shield, preventing wind from reaching the garden.
Volunteers gather at the beach and collect rubbish after the storm.
